items.title: Kent Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 22, 2006
items.q: Or think about it, think about Red Garland, Wynton Kelly, Bill Evans, Stan Getz, you know I mean you could have like, that was such an interesting thing to me because they’re learning the same information but wow I could tell Dexter from Sonny from Trane from Sonny Stitt.

ctx.x: Well that’s an interesting thing and I thought about that a lot. That’s an interesting theory in the stock market if you know, if you ever dabble in that, and that theory is all of the information is already priced. Everybody’s given the same information at the same time. So the means is always constant. There’s no new information being introduced. So the only way that you can really make money in the market is you have to make it by mistake. Somebody has to make a mistake. You see where I’m going? So all these…

out if you want, I mean just go and say what did you learn at Berklee? Or what did you learn at UC or what did you learn in Miami or what did you learn and what did you learn and what did you learn. Consequently, you’ll be surprised, and I’ve done it in an anecdotal kind of a way. And basically everybody’s learning the same information. Now there’s something good in that but what you have to do is you have to sort of take that information and how do you take that and make it your own thing? In other words there’s…
You know what I miss partly, that I think had something to with learning about people is reading the back of record jackets.
